scenes.headline: Turn observations into context.
scenes.subtitle: Threat Surface Area Assessment Tool (TSAAT)
scenes.body: TSAAT brings recorded observations about the cyber terrain together into a context aware data set.

scenes.headline: See the connected terrain.
scenes.subtitle: Devices. Software. Networks. Services.
scenes.body: Explore how configuration items and ICT systems connect to mission services and business services.

scenes.headline: Govern the cyber posture.
scenes.subtitle: Defence Cyber Terrain (DCT)
scenes.body: TSAAT assists cyber teams in governing the cyber posture of the Defence Cyber Terrain and reducing the threat surface area of networks and ICT systems.

scenes.headline: Understand. Investigate. Report.
scenes.subtitle: Put the observations to work
scenes.body: Understand the cyber terrain, investigate an issue or finding, and turn insights into a report.

scenes.subtitle: The foundation
scenes.body: OPORD/01-2019 starts CMDB and dynamic discovery. An enterprise platform reaches DPE and DSE by June 2022.

scenes.headline: Q3 2022
scenes.subtitle: Make the connections
scenes.body: Configuration Management processes are established, including ICT System Modelling.

scenes.subtitle: Assess the critical systems
scenes.body: DSR: HICTO orders 66 and 67 assess about 87 critical ICT Systems against 28 compliance questions. TSAAT v1.0 reports the findings.

scenes.subtitle: Scale the inventory
scenes.body: DIIS captures ICT System inventory and ownership. OMWOW models about 3,000 systems. TSAAT v2.0 and training arrive in Q4 2025.

scenes.headline: Q1 2026
scenes.subtitle: A wider conversation
scenes.body: TSAAT is presented to DSOC and Cyber Command as a reporting tool for visibility of the Cyber Terrain.

scenes.headline: Jan 2027
scenes.subtitle: The next chapter - planned
scenes.body: TSAAT v3.0 is designed in Q4 2026 for DSOC needs, with delivery planned for January 2027.

scenes.headline: See the whole terrain.
scenes.subtitle: An illustrative topology
scenes.body: Mission services and business services depend on ICT systems, networks and configuration items, or CIs.

scenes.headline: Inspect the building blocks.
scenes.subtitle: Devices + installed software
scenes.body: Servers, workstations and other CIs form the technical foundation. Blue SW icons identify software installed on servers.

scenes.headline: Follow the connections.
scenes.subtitle: Multiple networks + ICT systems
scenes.body: Communication paths connect CIs across networks. Recorded system membership gives those components a shared purpose.

scenes.headline: Connect to service purpose.
scenes.subtitle: Mission services + business services
scenes.body: Follow dependencies to see which systems support each service. Select a layer in the guide, or highlight all components.

scenes.headline: A finding is a starting point.
scenes.subtitle: Security vulnerabilities
scenes.body: A vulnerability observation records a potential weakness associated with a device or software.

scenes.headline: Add the context.
scenes.subtitle: Which device? Which software?
scenes.body: Examine the affected records, recorded CVE details and the source that reported the observation.

scenes.headline: Separate signal from proof.
scenes.subtitle: Observation is not exploitation
scenes.body: A recorded finding is not proof that a weakness is exploitable or has been exploited.

scenes.headline: Investigate. Then prioritise.
scenes.subtitle: Evidence supports judgement
scenes.body: Trace D3 to System B, Mission service A and Business service B. Validate the evidence and service relevance before deciding on action.

scenes.headline: An endpoint sees an address.
scenes.subtitle: Scenario 1 / Current example
scenes.body: Known endpoint D3 reports communication with 192.0.2.87, which has no matching endpoint record.

scenes.headline: A network device communicates.
scenes.subtitle: Scenario 2 / Network device
scenes.body: Known network device ND1 communicates with unmatched address 198.51.100.64. Keep the two endpoints separate.

scenes.headline: Discovery finds an unknown type.
scenes.subtitle: Scenario 3 / CMDB discovery scan
scenes.body: CMDB discovery scans an IP range and detects 192.0.2.47, but cannot classify it as a Server, Computer, Printer or Router.

scenes.headline: Investigate the gap.
scenes.subtitle: Identify. Classify. Validate.
scenes.body: Check the source and evidence, then establish identity, device type and ownership. An unknown address is not proof of malicious activity.

scenes.headline: A device issue. Business context.
scenes.subtitle: D1 / ICT System A
scenes.body: D1 belongs to System A. Business services A and B depend on that system, so review both services.

scenes.headline: Shared mission support.
scenes.subtitle: D5 / ICT System C
scenes.body: D5 belongs to System C, which supports Mission services A and B. Mission service A also depends on System B.

scenes.headline: A device link is unavailable.
scenes.subtitle: D7 / D3
scenes.body: The link joins D7 in System A and D3 in System B. Review Business services A and B and Mission service A, and check alternative paths.

scenes.headline: Review does not mean outage.
scenes.subtitle: Validate with the service owner
scenes.body: Confirm the recorded dependencies, alternative paths and current service state before concluding that a service is affected.

reporting.label: Watch observations become a focused report.

scenes.headline: Filter. Build. Share the rows.
scenes.subtitle: Filtered Excel
scenes.body: Start with the header scope, apply Explorer search, then export every matching row across all pages. Here, searching for D5 includes D5.

scenes.headline: Scope. Summarise. Brief the terrain.
scenes.subtitle: Briefing PDF
scenes.body: Keep every device in the applied header scope and loaded snapshot. The briefing includes D5 and D6 in System C, even when Explorer search shows only D5.

scenes.headline: Start. Trace. Share the evidence.
scenes.subtitle: Impact PDF
scenes.body: Follow a starting CI through its ICT system to dependent services. Package the full traced graph and supporting evidence with the selected scope and snapshot.

benefits.label: A clearer picture. A better conversation.

scenes.headline: See what you have.
scenes.subtitle: Visibility
scenes.body: Bring recorded inventory, relationships and observations into a view people can explore.

scenes.headline: Find the questions.
scenes.subtitle: Investigation
scenes.body: Spot missing details and follow the evidence behind summaries and findings.

scenes.headline: Share the understanding.
scenes.subtitle: Communication
scenes.body: Use consistent views, reports and exports to discuss the same evidence.

scenes.headline: Know the terrain. Take the next step.
scenes.subtitle: Explore the TSAAT Feature Guide
scenes.body: Choose a feature, learn how it works and practise using the guide.
